data.title: Stablecoin remittances cost 84% less than traditional transfers, report finds
data.description:
Stablecoin-funded remittances continue to offer substantial cost savings over traditional money transfers, particularly in emerging markets, reinforcing one of the leading use cases for digital dollars as payment activity grows.

According to a new third-quarter report from Borderless.xyz, a stablecoin payments network, sending a $200 remittance through stablecoin-funded payment rails costs a median of 1%, or $2, compared with 6.36%, or $12.72, for traditional remittances, based on World Bank data.

The difference makes stablecoin-funded remittances roughly 84% cheaper, although the comparison uses Borderless’s third-quarter 2026 pricing and World Bank figures from the same period in 2025.

The savings are also substantial across emerging markets. In Sub-Saharan Africa, stablecoin-funded remittances cost 2.9%, compared with 8.46% for traditional transfers. In Latin America, the costs are 1.25% and 5.64%, respectively.

Business payments made through stablecoins are also significantly cheaper, according to the report. A $10,000 stablecoin-funded transfer to the eurozone costs as little as $26 when routed through the lowest-cost provider, compared with $52 across all corridors at the median provider.

By comparison, a traditional international bank wire costs between $135 and $150 for the same amount, including transfer fees and an assumed 1% foreign-exchange margin.

Stablecoins offer significant cost savings on larger business transactions. Source: Borderless.xyz

Stablecoin payouts settle in minutes, but reliability varies

Beyond cost savings, the Borderless report found that stablecoin-funded payments can reach recipients’ local bank accounts in minutes, depending on the payment network used.

In Brazil, payouts through the PIX network settled in a median of two minutes during the third quarter, while Mexico’s SPEI network took three minutes. Colombia’s PSE network also recorded a median settlement time of two minutes.

By comparison, traditional SWIFT transfers typically settled the next business day, with the slowest 10% taking three business days.

However, payment completion rates varied considerably. Mexico’s SPEI network successfully completed 98.6% of payouts, followed by Brazil’s PIX at 97.8%. Colombia’s PSE network completed 79%, while Costa Rica’s SINPE recorded a completion rate of just 73%.

The findings come as stablecoin transaction activity continues to grow. Standard Chartered recently highlighted rising transaction volumes despite relatively flat growth in the overall stablecoin market capitalization this year. The bank expects the market to reach $2 trillion by 2030, two years later than its previous forecast.

data.title: Tesla Stocks Rise Although Roadster Reveal Leaves Pricing and Volume Unset
data.description:

The immediate earnings story runs through products already selling. Tesla's October 2 operating update reported 486,532 quarterly vehicle deliveries, including 478,237 Model 3 and Model Y vehicles, alongside 13.7 gigawatt-hours of energy-storage deployments. Those two vehicle models accounted for roughly 98.3% of deliveries. Their margins, together with storage profitability and cash generation, give investors concrete numbers to scrutinize when third-quarter financial results arrive after the October 21 market close.

Valuation adds another hurdle. The chart places the share price 8.38% above the GF Value estimate of $336.28, suggesting the stock already carries a premium to that benchmark. The market snapshot provides additional trading context, but the next financial test is straightforward: whether Tesla's existing businesses can produce earnings that support its valuation while investors wait for the Roadster.

data.title: CDC reports 4,410 measles cases as outbreak grows
data.description:
The US CDC on Friday reported 4,410 measles cases nationwide as of October 15, an increase of 330 from its last update a week ago, as an outbreak of the highly contagious disease continues.

Here are key details:

  • Measles-related hospitalizations this year stand at 451, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said

  • The state of Pennsylvania has reported five measles-related deaths

  • The CDC has confirmed two measles-associated deaths in 2026, though it has not identified the states involved

  • Pennsylvania has reported 1,260 measles cases this year as of October 16, with 238 disease-related hospitalizations, according to state health department data

  • Last month, the CDC shifted to using mortality data from the National Center for Health Statistics for measles-related deaths, rather than relying on state health departments, a change that has drawn scrutiny

  • The CDC said on Tuesday it would deploy more support to Pennsylvania to help investigate the outbreak

  • Children and teenagers aged 5 to 19 were the largest group affected by the disease at 1,856, or 42% of cases, followed by adults aged 20 and older at 1,787 cases, or 41%, CDC data showed

  • Earlier this month, the state of New York declared a disaster emergency for the measles outbreak, the first such declaration by a US state

data.title: The NBA bans certain types of parlay bets with its sportsbook partners
data.description:
The NBA sent a memo to partner sportsbooks prohibiting certain types of bets this season. The league has the authority to restrict betting types through its agreements. Going forward, bettors will not be able to include the under on the same player's statistics in parlays. The league also directed sportsbooks to not offer bets on the winner of the opening tip, players to miss specific shots, and under bets on players who are expected to play fewer than 12 minutes in a specific game.

"There's a balance between ensuring that we are removing problematic bet types but also ensuring that we don't just move activity into the illegal market," NBA executive vice president Scott Kaufman-Ross told ESPN. The league thinks the new restrictions strike the right balance.

The NBA has seen a few players wrapped up in betting legal cases. Jontay Porter, formerly of the Toronto Raptors, pleaded guilty in July 2024 to conspiracy to commit wire fraud. He admitted deliberately leaving games early to help bettors win wagers that his statistics would fall below sportsbook thresholds. The NBA banned him for life. Terry Rozier was charged in October 2025 with wire fraud and money laundering conspiracies. Prosecutors allege he tipped off associates that he would exit a March 2023 game early, enabling more than $200K in “under” bets. He has pleaded not guilty.

The impact is negative for DraftKings and FanDuel since parlay bets have higher margins or hold rates that traditional sports bets. DraftKings was down 1.1% in afternoon trading, while FanDuel owner Flutter Entertainment was up 0.1%.

data.title: Star Oil Trader Who Made Wrong-Way Bet to Leave Vitol — WSJ
data.description:
By Rebecca Feng and Peter Rudegeair

Yaoyao Liu, a star oil trader who found himself deep in the hole on a bet made at the start of the Iran war, is set to leave commodities giant Vitol, people familiar with the matter said.

Liu and his team took a several-hundred-million-dollar hit earlier this year after a wrong way bet on diesel and crude prices, The Wall Street Journal reported in April. Some of the losses were quickly made up.

His team's mark-to-market losses sent shock waves through the close-knit trading industry, where Liu was known for his big, and often lucrative, wagers on financial contracts tied to underlying energy markets.

Liu is expected to leave Vitol by the end of the year, according to the people familiar with the matter. One of the people said he is leaving for family reasons.

Liu's trade was a rare misstep at a moment of opportunity in the oil trading world. Several of Vitol's peers, including rivals Trafigura and the trading arms of BP and TotalEnergies, have profited from the disruptions caused by the war in Iran. Privately held Vitol hasn't disclosed financial results for the current year. In April, a person familiar with the matter said Vitol was up for the year despite Liu's trades.

A Vitol spokesperson declined to comment.

Liu made outsize profits for Vitol, where he was one of the leaders on the trading floor. In 2020, Liu and his team made billions of dollars in gains for Vitol betting that the impact of the pandemic on the oil market would be short-lived, people familiar with the matter said.

Liu's big bets were an object of fascination among oil traders and brokers, many of whom tried to mimic his moves and profit on his prescience.

Born in China, Liu graduated from Cambridge University where he published a paper on quantum chemistry. He joined Vitol in 2012 after a stint at Goldman Sachs.

Within Vitol, Liu led a team of analysts and traders in Dubai, London and Houston. While colleagues at the commodity trader mainly move physical tankers of crude and fuel or trade electricity and natural gas, Liu's team wagers on financial contracts tied to underlying energy markets.

At the start of the Iran war, his team made large bets that diesel prices would rise relative to jet fuel, and that Dubai crude would fall in price compared with the global benchmark, Brent crude.

Those positions stood to benefit if President Trump pulled back from a military buildup that sent jitters through energy markets early in the year. Instead, when the war started and Iran shut the Strait of Hormuz, Liu's trades went bad as price moves cut against him.

Liu hasn't been actively trading since the summer, according to the people familiar with the matter.

London-based Vitol plays a crucial role connecting energy producers in far-flung corners of the world with customers. It handled about 8 million barrels of crude oil and oil products a day last year, enough to supply Japan, Germany, France and the U.K. combined. In 2025, Vitol had $343 billion in revenue, more than ExxonMobil.

Write to Rebecca Feng at rebecca.feng@wsj.com and Peter Rudegeair at peter.rudegeair@wsj.com

data.title: SA Asks: Are neocloud stocks a buy after this week's sell-off? (Update)
data.description:
Are neocloud stocks a buy after this week's sell-off?

Seeking Alpha analysts Danil Sereda, Petri Dish Reports, and Carla Magliocco weigh in.

Danil Sereda: In a recent article, I compared Nebius and CoreWeave to find the future outperformer, and following the sell-off that we're seeing now in both of them, I'm not changing my opinion that Nebius looks superior in the long run.

First, it's the management team. Nebius has a CEO who built Yandex, the biggest tech conglomerate in the CIS region, and one of the biggest in Eurasia in general. The team is very experienced, and Nebius holds a massive advantage over CoreWeave in terms of labor costs and flexibility.

Second, their balance sheet remains quite strong. I know it's going to take on incremental debt in the next few years, but I like the way management structures the new debt loads and attracts money through convertibles or direct stakes from Nvidia and others.

If we recall why neocloud stocks are dropping so much, we'll find that it was due to Gartner predicting that ~80% of neoclouds will evaporate by 2030. Nebius is unlikely to be one of those evaporated companies, in my opinion. Not in a today-like environment of rising demand for AI workloads and all that.

Coming back to the main question, I'd like to answer that not all neclouds deserve a Buy rating on the dip. Nebius deserves it for the reasons I listed above. CoreWeave doesn't, because its debt levels look extreme, and the odds of evaporating are mathematically higher. At least that's how I see the setup.

Ex-miners such as IREN , Cipher Digital , or Wolfspeed are also not Buys because they seem to lack the superior tech filling that Nebius and CoreWeave have. They're mainly just selling GPU compute, where the asset base is at risk of becoming obsolete. Neclouds need to have SaaS-filling and tech features to give customers more offerings and make sure their workloads don't break at some point. Small ex-miners don't seem to be capable of doing that, in my opinion.

In short, I'd only go with Nebius on this dip and ignore all other tickers.

(Danil Sereda leads the SA investing group Beyond the Wall Investing.)

Petri Dish Reports: The Gartner report had a big impact on market sentiment. My main argument is that we should treat AI infrastructure demand and neocloud shareholder returns as two completely different investment questions. The reality is that the industry is going to expand pretty rapidly, while some infrastructure providers struggle with financing costs, GPU depreciation, or even weak margins and dilution.

When we compare big players like CoreWeave , Nebius , Iren , and Applied Digital , we need to focus on three areas.

First, who captures the economics? We have to compare their contract pricing, margins, and differentiation rather than simply relying on a player's backlog figure or projected revenue.

Second, who can actually finance their growth sustainably? Debt obligations, cash flow, and construction costs are going to have an impact.

Lastly, who owns assets that actually retain value? What I mean by this is that we need to distinguish GPU-dependent businesses from companies whose economics are tied to land, power, and some hefty long-term data center leases.

Everyone realizes that choosing which company will win is the hard part here, but first we should understand that treating all neoclouds as one investment category is going to overlook some very meaningful differences in their business models and financing risks.

Carla Magliocco: The market is going through a panic spiral in AI similar to the one we saw in the last week of July. And where there's panic, buy! I took the opportunity to expand my position in Nebius .

It's true that this time the economic factors are more deteriorated than in July, especially because taking on debt for big investments has become more expensive. All equities are suffering in this context, and AI is suffering as well. But the cost of debt hits neoclouds such as Nebius , CoreWeave , Hut 8 , and IREN harder, because their growth models depend on large expenditures by hyperscalers. Remember, however, that this context calls into question the financing capacity, not the development nor the profitability of AI.

That’s why now is the time to stay calm and put any available liquidity, big or small, to work. And those who have no more liquidity, just hold your position. Neoclouds offer a key and highly specialized service for AI hardware: computing power. If you have doubts about this thesis, where the expected returns in this bottleneck are huge, selling wouldn’t be the best alternative.

data.title: US energy firms left the rig count unchanged this week, Baker Hughes says
data.description:
By Scott DiSavino

US energy firms left the rig count unchanged this week with oil rigs down and natural gas and miscellaneous rigs up, energy services firm Baker Hughes said in its closely followed report on Friday.

The total oil and gas rig count, an early indicator of future output, held steady at 603 in the week to October 16. (BHGUSWTT), (BHGUSOILDRLW), (BHGUSGASDRLW) (USOIRC=ECI), (USGSRC=ECI)

Baker Hughes said that put the total rig count up 55 rigs, or 10% above this time last year.

Baker Hughes said oil rigs fell by three to 459 this week, while gas rigs rose by one to 133, and other miscellaneous rigs rose by two to 11, the highest since January.

The oil and gas rig count declined by 7% in 2025, 5% in 2024, and 20% in 2023 as lower US oil prices prompted energy firms to focus more on boosting shareholder returns and paying down debt rather than increasing output.

But now with spot US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude prices expected to rise in 2026 for the first time in four years due to supply disruptions from the Iran war, the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) projected that crude output will rise from a record 13.7 million barrels per day (bpd) in 2025 to 13.9 million bpd in 2026.

On the gas side, EIA projected output will jump from a record 107.6 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) in 2025 to 112.2 bcfd in 2026 as demand for the fuel rises to produce electricity for power-hungry data centers and liquefied natural gas (LNG) for export.

Latest highlights are led by a 2025 Ferrari Daytona SP3 (Estimate: $16,000,000 - $18,000,000), chassis number 314846, finished in the exquisite Tailor Made shade of Verde Francesca over a two-tone Nero Alcantara and Mustard Aunde Jeans interior. Offered from its original owner, the curator of an exceptional private collection, the SP3 is one of just 600 examples produced and displays just 81 miles at cataloging. The second model in Ferrari’s sought after “Icona” series, the Daytona SP3 is many things—a rolling tribute to one of the marque’s most triumphant afternoons, a showcase of naturally aspirated engineering at its peak, and quite possibly the final chapter in a mid-engine, naturally aspirated lineage that began nearly sixty years ago. The car on offer is equipped with numerous carbon fiber elements, airbrushed fender shield, a suspension lifter, and a full complement of factory accessories.

“The collector car market has quickly recognized the significance of the Daytona SP3 in Ferrari’s history,” says Barney Ruprecht, Vice President of Auctions for Broad Arrow. “In the few short years since the SP3's reveal, values have climbed sharply, reflecting both the model's extreme exclusivity, and a growing understanding that it may represent the final expression Ferrari’s naturally aspirated V12 for the road. This is a particularly special example of the 600 made, with a bespoke specification that’s sure to appeal to today’s most discerning collectors.”

Additional thrilling Ferrari highlights coming to Broad Arrow Las Vegas Auction include:

2014 Ferrari LaFerrari (Estimate: $8,500,000 - $10,000,000)

This is a low-mileage, extensively specified example of the first hybrid hypercar from Maranello, producing a combined 950 horsepower from its 6.3-liter V12 hybrid powerplant. One of approximately 120 examples delivered new to the US, the LaFerrari on offer is finished in iconic Rosso Corsa over Nero leather with Rosso accents, recently serviced, and accompanied by its battery charger, fitted car cover, and tool kit. It is offered with a two-year Certified Pre-Owned warranty, including coverage of its hybrid battery, valid through October 2028.

2003 Ferrari Enzo (Estimate: $6,500,000 - $8,500,000)

One of only 111 delivered new to the US market, this true driver’s example of Ferrari’s singular turn-of-the-century hypercar shows under 18,000 miles at cataloging. It has been refinished by Carrozzeria Zanasi in Maranello to its original Rosso Corsa and features a Pelle Nera interior. Classiche certified and serviced in 2026 by Ferrari Dallas at a cost exceeding $10,000, this is an eminently usable example of the iconic hypercar that carries the legacy of Enzo Ferrari, prepared to be enjoyed the way its namesake intended.

2011 Ferrari 599 SA Aperta (Estimate: $4,100,000 - $4,500,000)

This exceptionally rare supercar is one of only 80 special series SA Aperta models produced in celebration of Pininfarina’s 80th anniversary. Finished in classic Rosso Corsa over Nero leather with Rosso details, it is offered in near-new condition with just 745 miles, $87,000 in optional extras, and an exhilarating zero-to-62 miles per hour time of 3.6 seconds with a top speed of 202 miles per hour.

Additional modern collectible Ferraris on offer include the just-announced 106-mile time capsule 1997 Ferrari F50, a 2015 Ferrari 458 Speciale A offered without reserve, a 2015 Ferrari 458 Speciale, a 2001 Ferrari 550 Barchetta Pininfarina, and more. View the more than 25 Ferraris on offer in the Las Vegas Auction here.

Following the fantastic results for many Ferrari supercars at Broad Arrow recent Zoute Concours Auction, the company continues its momentum in Europe with its second annual Zürich Auction on November 7, the official auction partner of the renowned Auto Zürich show. Exceptional Ferraris are set for the sale at the Dolder Grand hotel, including two of the market’s most desirable models, offered without reserve.

2015 Ferrari LaFerrari (Estimate: CHF 5'500'000 - CHF 7'500'000 | Offered Without Reserve)

Striking in Bianco Fuji over a Bianchi/Neri leather interior, the LaFerrari on offer in Zürich is one of approximately 50 examples specified with the exposed carbon-fiber roof. This delivery-mileage example is offered with the common “sticky buttons” issue remedied and with a new high-voltage battery. The LaFerrari is a well-cared-for example of an essential acquisition—one of the most significant Ferraris ever built.

2017 Ferrari F12tdf (Estimate: CHF 1'300'000 - CHF 1'500'000 | Offered Without Reserve)

The F12tdf was the last Ferrari model to be styled in collaboration with Pininfarina and features a 6.3-litre V12, the most powerful naturally aspirated V12 when it was introduced. This particular car was delivered new to Switzerland finished in distinctive special-order matte Alluminio Opaco over Nero Alcantara with matter carbon fiber and Giallo accents throughout. Offered with just two owners and 13,601 kilometers from new, this is a recently serviced, compelling example of a highly coveted Ferrari.

View the more than 13 Ferraris on offer in Broad Arrow’s Zürich Auction here.

Broad Arrow Private Sales has connected the buyers and sellers of many of the most in-demand Ferrari supercars in recent months, with successful sales throughout its international network. Recent results include two desirable “non-cat, non-adjust” examples of the iconic F40 supercar in both the US and the UK, a 2024 Ferrari Daytona SP3 in a stunning Atelier specification of Extrarange Nero DS Opaco with Gloss Black wheels, and a superbly preserved 2004 Ferrari Enzo with an unbroken chain of Japanese documentation. Learn more about Broad Arrow Private Sales at broadarrowprivatesales.com.

The market for modern Ferrari supercars is looking stronger than ever, and Broad Arrow is proud to be entrusted by both buyers and sellers to secure new homes for these spectacular pieces of motoring history. Those interested in the sale or purchase of a Ferrari through either Broad Arrow Auctions or Private Sales are invited to contact a Broad Arrow Car Specialist via info@broadarrowauctions.com or by calling +1 313-312-0780 in North America or +44-2045-920-16 in EMEA.

Further details, high-res images, and interviews with Broad Arrow Executives and Specialists available on request.

data.title: Shell to sell French fuel stations to DCC Energy - Reuters
data.description:
Shell has reached a deal with Ireland-based DCC Energy for the proposed ​sale of its network of fuel retail stations and related ‌transport fuel services in France, Reuters reported Friday, without providing financial details.

A deal has not been finalized, ​although completion is expected in Q2 2027, subject ​to consultation with employee representatives, according to the report, which also said the transaction would include ~70 sites, eight LNG installations, and the transfer of 35 employees.

DCC Energy reportedly would operate the stations under a long-term Shell brand license, but Shell's core fuel supply operations would be excluded, ​meaning the ⁠buyer would source its fuel independently.

DCC Energy serves millions of customers across the industrial and public sectors and delivers off-grid energy solutions, led by liquid gas, the company's website ​said.

data.title: Hitachi Energy and Rockwell Automation unite power and automation to help industries accelerate electrification
data.description:
Zurich and Milwaukee, WI, Oct 16, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - Hitachi Energy, a global leader in electrification, and Rockwell Automation, Inc. (NYSE: ROK), the world's largest company dedicated to industrial automation and digital transformation, announced today a collaboration centered on an integrated grid-to-process architecture that combines the infrastructure powering industrial facilities with the systems that manage production.

As industrial companies face rising power demand, growing pressure to decarbonize, and increasing constraints on capital investment, electrical systems and production operations can no longer be planned in isolation. Decisions about power infrastructure increasingly influence operational performance, while production requirements play a larger role in planning, deploying, and operating electrical systems.

By bringing together expertise in grid connection, power quality, energy management, protection and control, process automation, and digital operations, Hitachi Energy and Rockwell Automation aim to help customers achieve a more seamless integration of grid and process systems. Planning power and production systems together can streamline engineering, improve cross-functional coordination, and support digital mining operations, while exploring scalable and modular approaches that can support future expansion and evolving electrification requirements.

Mining and metals will serve as the initial focus of the collaboration. As demand for critical minerals grow, mining companies must simultaneously expand production, modernize operations, and accelerate the electrification of their own facilities. Analysis estimates that growth capital expenditures for new capacity could require $1 trillion USD over the next decade*1. Reliable, high-quality power is fundamental to these operations, particularly in energy-intensive processes such as crushing, grinding, conveying, and processing, where disruptions can affect equipment utilization, production continuity, and operating costs.*1 McKinsey & Co. Report, "The capex crystal ball: Beating the odds in mining project delivery," Predicting cost and schedule overruns in mining | McKinsey, November 2024.

"Electrification is changing the economics of industrial operations. Decisions about energy infrastructure increasingly influence productivity, sustainability, and growth," says Marco Berardi, Head of Grid & Power Quality Solutions and Service at Hitachi Energy. "As industries expand capacity and modernize their operations, they need greater coordination between the systems that power their facilities and the processes that drive production. By bringing together the strengths of Hitachi Energy and Rockwell Automation, we can help customers navigate this complexity, improve operational performance, and support more efficient, resilient, and sustainable industrial operations."

"The future of industry will be defined by how effectively companies integrate energy and production," said Brian Holte, vice president, Global Industry Growth, Rockwell Automation. "By combining Hitachi Energy's leadership in electrification with Rockwell Automation's experience in automation and digital transformation, we help customers design, build, and operate more intelligent, resilient, and sustainable sites. Together, we are enabling a grid-to-process approach that improves performance, accelerates growth, and helps customers bring new manufacturing capacity online faster, more predictably, and at greater scale."

Once facilities are operational, the combination of electrification, automation, and digital technologies can provide greater visibility across energy consumption, production performance, and asset utilization. The approach also provides a scalable foundation for future capacity expansion, increased electrification, and the integration of new energy resources.

The companies are exploring opportunities in solution development, customer engagement, and selected industrial applications. While initially focused on mining and metals, the companies see broader potential across other energy-intensive industries.

About Hitachi Energy

Hitachi Energy is a global leader in electrification, powering the electricity era to meet the energy demands of today, and the next 25 years. As the energy arm of Hitachi Group, over three billion people depend on our pioneering, mission critical technologies to power their daily lives. With over a century of innovation, we are addressing the most urgent energy challenge of our time: driving the evolution of the world's energy system to ensure abundant, secure, affordable, and sustainable power for today's generation and the next. With an unparalleled installed base in over 140 countries, we are the grid ecosystem partner across the utility, industry, data center, and transportation sectors. Headquartered in Switzerland, we employ over 56,000 people in 60 countries and generate revenues of around $20 billion USD.

About Hitachi, Ltd.

Through its Social Innovation Business (SIB) that brings together IT, OT(Operational Technology) and products, Hitachi aims to be a global leader in continuously transforming social infrastructure through digital, contributing to a harmonized society where the environment, wellbeing, and economic growth are in balance. Hitachi operates worldwide across four sectors - Digital Systems & Services, Energy, Mobility, and Connective Industries - as well as a Strategic SIB Business Unit focused on new growth areas. With Lumada at its core, Hitachi creates value by combining data, technology and domain knowledge to solve customer and social challenges. Revenues for FY2025 (ended March 31, 2026) totaled 10,586.7 billion yen, with 606 consolidated subsidiaries and approximately 290,000 employees worldwide. Visit us at www.hitachi.com.
